concepts.name: Manual versus code-defined infrastructure
concepts.summary: Explain why defining resources in files is more repeatable and auditable than configuring them by hand in a console.

concepts.name: Declarative versus imperative styles
concepts.summary: Distinguish describing the desired end state from scripting the steps to reach it.

concepts.name: Resources and their attributes
concepts.summary: Recognise that a configuration is made of resources of a given type with named attributes, such as a virtual machine or a network.

concepts.name: Configuration files in version control
concepts.summary: Understand that infrastructure code is stored in Git so changes are tracked, reviewed and reversible.

concepts.name: Plan then apply workflow
concepts.summary: Describe the cycle of writing code, previewing the proposed changes and then applying them.

concepts.name: Reproducible environments
concepts.summary: Explain how the same code can create identical dev, test and production environments.

misconceptions.text: Infrastructure as code is just a shell script that runs commands in order.
Once infrastructure is written as code, nobody needs to understand the underlying cloud services.
Applying the code twice will create two copies of every resource.

concepts.name: Input variables and outputs
concepts.summary: Parameterise a configuration with variables and expose values such as addresses through outputs.

concepts.name: Idempotency
concepts.summary: Explain and observe that re-applying unchanged code leaves infrastructure unchanged.

concepts.name: State as record of reality
concepts.summary: Understand that the tool keeps state mapping code resources to real resources and uses it to compute changes.

concepts.name: Reading a change plan
concepts.summary: Interpret a plan to identify what will be created, updated or destroyed.

concepts.name: Resource dependencies
concepts.summary: Use references between resources so they are created in the correct order.

concepts.name: Provider configuration and authentication
concepts.summary: Configure a provider and authenticate it to a cloud account with limited permissions.

concepts.name: Secrets kept out of code
concepts.summary: Keep passwords and keys out of committed files by using environment variables or a secrets store.

misconceptions.text: Editing a resource in the cloud console is harmless because the code will simply pick up the change.
If the plan shows a change, it only modifies the resource in place.
Private repositories make it safe to commit secrets in configuration files.

concepts.name: Reusable modules
concepts.summary: Package related resources into modules with clear inputs and outputs and reuse them across configurations.

concepts.name: Remote state and locking
concepts.summary: Store state in a shared backend with locking so teams do not corrupt it by concurrent runs.

concepts.name: Environment separation
concepts.summary: Structure code and state to isolate dev, staging and production while sharing common modules.

concepts.name: Configuration drift
concepts.summary: Detect and analyse differences between declared and actual infrastructure and decide how to reconcile them.

concepts.name: Importing existing resources
concepts.summary: Bring manually created resources under code management without recreating them.

concepts.name: Pipeline-driven changes
concepts.summary: Run validation, plan and apply through a pipeline with pull request review.

concepts.name: Replacement versus in-place update
concepts.summary: Analyse which attribute changes force resource replacement and their impact on data and availability.

misconceptions.text: Copying the same configuration folder for each environment is as maintainable as using shared modules.
Storing state in the Git repository is the best way to share it with the team.
Drift only happens when someone is careless, so it does not need monitoring.

concepts.name: Automated infrastructure testing
concepts.summary: Combine static analysis, unit-style checks and ephemeral integration deployments to catch defects before production.

concepts.name: Policy as code
concepts.summary: Evaluate and encode security and cost rules that automatically block non-compliant changes.

concepts.name: State blast radius design
concepts.summary: Judge how to split state and stacks by lifecycle, ownership and risk to limit the impact of a bad change.

concepts.name: Module versioning and contracts
concepts.summary: Assess module interface stability and use versioning to roll out changes safely across consumers.

concepts.name: Safe refactoring of live infrastructure
concepts.summary: Restructure code and move resources in state without causing destruction or recreation.

concepts.name: Immutable versus mutable infrastructure
concepts.summary: Evaluate replacing resources against patching them in place, and how image building and configuration management fit in.

concepts.name: Zero-downtime rollout strategies
concepts.summary: Analyse lifecycle rules and deployment patterns that change infrastructure without interrupting service.

misconceptions.text: A successful plan guarantees the apply will succeed and behave correctly.
One large state for everything is simplest and therefore safest.
Renaming a resource in code is purely cosmetic.

concepts.name: Multi-account governance architecture
concepts.summary: Create an account, permission and pipeline structure that scales across teams, regions and possibly providers.

concepts.name: Platform engineering with IaC
concepts.summary: Design paved-road modules and self-service workflows that let teams provision safely without central bottlenecks.

concepts.name: Tool selection trade-offs
concepts.summary: Evaluate declarative DSLs, general-purpose-language tools and cloud-native templates against organisational needs.

concepts.name: State security and recovery
concepts.summary: Evaluate protection, access control and recovery procedures for state that contains sensitive data.

concepts.name: Custom providers and extensions
concepts.summary: Build providers or extensions that manage resources from APIs not covered by existing tooling.

concepts.name: Continuous reconciliation and automated remediation
concepts.summary: Design systems that continuously compare and correct actual state against declared intent, with human override.

concepts.name: Migration of legacy estates
concepts.summary: Judge sequencing, risk and tooling for bringing a large manually built estate under code incrementally.

misconceptions.text: Automatic remediation of all drift is always desirable.
Adopting one IaC tool across the whole organisation removes the need for governance and conventions.
Legacy estates should be imported in one big-bang effort to reach full coverage quickly.
